sections.heading: Scope And Safety
sections.body: Body astrology is a symbolic correspondence layer only. It is not health advice, not nutritional advice, not a remedy system, and not a way to identify or explain body concerns. Always use 'traditionally associated with' for the seven visible planets and sign correspondences, and 'modern overlay associated with' for Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto. For any body or health concern, direct the user to a licensed professional.

sections.heading: Excluded By Design
sections.body: Do not include supplement, vitamin, herb, flower essence, tea, diet, remedy, or protocol tables in the app. The knowledge base may store symbolic body correspondences, but it must not give instructions about what a user should consume, avoid, apply, or do for a body concern.

sections.heading: Planet Correspondences
sections.body: Use these as symbolic planet-body associations only. Do not turn them into predictions, warnings, or care instructions.

items.label: Sun
items.body: Traditionally associated with vitality, core energy, and the body's central animating force.

items.label: Moon
items.body: Traditionally associated with upper digestion, bodily fluids, nourishment, and the body's changing rhythms.

items.label: Mercury
items.body: Traditionally associated with the brain, nervous system, coordination, and the body's communication channels.

items.label: Venus
items.body: Traditionally associated with softness, moisture, ease, the lymphatic layer, and relaxation in the body.

items.label: Mars
items.body: Traditionally associated with heat, urgency, sharpness, redness, activation, and fast-moving body symbolism.

items.label: Jupiter
items.body: Traditionally associated with growth, expansion, abundance, and excess as a symbolic body principle.

items.label: Saturn
items.body: Traditionally associated with structure, boundaries, dryness, restriction, bones, teeth, skin, and slow-moving body symbolism.

items.label: Uranus
items.body: Modern overlay associated with sudden shifts, irregular rhythms, electrical symbolism, and erratic nervous-system themes.

items.label: Neptune
items.body: Modern overlay associated with sensitivity, porous boundaries, diffusion, subtlety, and body experiences that feel hard to pin down.

items.label: Pluto
items.body: Modern overlay associated with deep release, elimination, regeneration symbolism, and hidden processes coming to the surface.

sections.heading: Sign Correspondences
sections.body: Use these as traditional sign-body correspondences only. They describe symbolic rulerships, not risk, certainty, or instruction.

items.label: Aries
items.body: Traditionally associated with the head, face, brain, eyes, and skull.

items.label: Taurus
items.body: Traditionally associated with the throat, neck, thyroid, and vocal cords.

items.label: Gemini
items.body: Traditionally associated with the lungs, arms, hands, shoulders, and nervous system.

items.label: Cancer
items.body: Traditionally associated with the chest, breasts, stomach, and upper digestive tract.

items.label: Leo
items.body: Traditionally associated with the heart, spine, upper back, and circulation.

items.label: Virgo
items.body: Traditionally associated with the intestines, digestive system, gut, and spleen.

items.label: Libra
items.body: Traditionally associated with the kidneys, lower back, adrenal glands, and skin.

items.label: Scorpio
items.body: Traditionally associated with the reproductive organs, bladder, and excretory system.

items.label: Sagittarius
items.body: Traditionally associated with the hips, thighs, liver, and sciatic nerve.

items.label: Capricorn
items.body: Traditionally associated with the bones, knees, joints, teeth, and skin.

items.label: Aquarius
items.body: Traditionally associated with the lower legs, ankles, calves, and circulation.

items.label: Pisces
items.body: Traditionally associated with the feet, lymphatic system, and immune system.

sections.heading: App Policy
sections.body: If shown in the app, label this as a symbolic body-correspondence layer. Do not display it in a way that implies a chart can determine, predict, or explain a person's health. Keep it separate from transit alerts, personal recommendations, and any feature that could be mistaken for care guidance.
